title: Integrated genomic and transcriptomic profiling dissects spatiotemporal evolution of metastatic hepatocellular carcinoma
study_description: Comprehensive molecular analysis of metastatic hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) is lacking. Here， we performed whole-exome and transcriptome sequencing of 269 primary， 114 intrahepatic recurrent， and 118 extrahepatic metastatic regions from 224 HCC patients and shed light on the complexity of HCC metastasis evolutionary trajectories and immune crosstalk， which laid foundation for elucidating mechanisms and the therapeutic vulnerabilities of metastatic HCC.

title: Integrated Genomic Analyses Identify High-Risk Factors Associated with Poor Outcomes of T-ALL
study_description: T-ALL is an aggressive hematologic malignancy and adult T-ALLs are often associated with poor outcomes. Recent large-scale genomic landscape studies have identified frequently mutated genes and dysregulated pathways in major subtypes of T-ALLs1-3. However， few of these large-scale genomic analyses contain survival-related data， which makes molecular-based prognosis and designs of new targeted therapies difficult. In this study， we performed integrated genomic and transcriptomic analyses on samples from 137 pediatric and adult T-ALL patients， of which 90% have outcome information. Out of 54 recurrently mutated genes， we identified poor outcome-associated mutations in EZH2， ASXL1， KRAS， IDH2， JAK3， RB1， KMT2C， TCF7 gene (high-risk gene) and in the RAS pathway. The status of the high-risk gene and RAS pathway mutation groups were independent predictors than factors related with age and clinical features. By combining public datasets， we demonstrated that Asian and adult T-ALLs had higher rates of high-risk gene and Ras pathway mutations than that of Caucasian and pediatric T-ALLs. We also found that differentially expressed genes in early T progenitor ALL (ETP ALL) subtype were largely controlled by the transcription factor PU.1 and that the PU.1-TIM3-GAL-9 regulatory loop was essential for the formation and maintenance of ETP ALL.

title: Immune Correlates of Response and Resistance to Neoadjuvant Chemo-immunotherapy in Non-small Cell Lung Cancer
study_description: To understand mechanisms of primary resistance， we followed a sufficiently large cohort of NSCLC patients receiving neoadjuvant immunotherapy， and profiled post-treatment samples using single-cell RNA and T cell receptor (TCR) sequencing. By associating tumor immune microenvironment (TIME) with response， we uncovered heterogeneous mechanisms of response and major mechanisms of primary resistance， providing insights into strategic developments of combination regimens.

title: Pharmacogenomic profiling of intra-tumor heterogeneity by a large organoid biobank of liver cancer
study_description: Inter- and intra-tumor heterogeneity is a major hurdle in primary liver cancer (PLC) precision therapy. Here， we established a PLC biobank， consisting of 399 organoids derived from 144 patients， which recapitulated histopathology and genomic landscape of parental tumors， and were reliable for drug sensitivity screening， evidenced by both in vivo models and patient response. Integrative analysis dissected PLC heterogeneity， regarding genomic， transcriptomic characteristics and sensitivity to seven clinically-relevant drugs， as well as clinical associations. Pharmacogenomic analysis identified and validated multi-gene expression signatures predicting drug response for better patient stratification. Furthermore， c-Jun was revealed as a major mediator to Lenvatinib resistance， through JNK and β-catenin signaling. A new compound (PKUF-01) comprising moieties of Lenvatinib and Veratramine (c-Jun inhibitor) was synthesized and screened， exhibiting a marked synergistic effect. Together， our study characterized the landscape of PLC heterogeneity， developed predictive biomarker panels， and revealed a novel Lenvatinib resistant mechanism for combinatory therapy.

title: Multi-omics integrative analysis of esophageal squamous carcinoma
study_description: In this study， we performed WGS， WGBS， RNA sequencing， and small RNA sequencing on tumor tissues as well as matched adjacent non-neoplastic tissues from  ESCC patients to discover potential molecular subgroups. We present a comprehensive molecular profiling of ESCC with a focus on identifying novel molecular subgroups and functionally altered signaling pathways that may drive tumorigenesis and serve as prognostic or therapeutic signatures.

title: Whole Genome Sequencing  in Esophageal Squamous Cell Carcinoma
study_description: In this project， we performed deep WGS in microneedle-punctured formalin fixed paraffin embedded tumor tissues and matched adjacent noncancerous specimens on a large set of ESCC patients with clinical follow up data. Herein， we classify ESCC into three main subtypes based on clinically relevant genomic alterations and implicate the association of these subtypes with outcomes of patients. Our genomic study uncovers an extensive landscape of driver genetic alterations across coding and noncoding regions， and defines their potential molecular pathology in ESCC.

title: Whole  exome sequencing  of patients with CRC from the Changkang project
study_description: Colorectal cancer (CRC) is a heterogeneous disease with high varieties in genetics， while the genomic basis of CRC and their clinical associations remain poorly understood. Aiming to establish a large genomic and clinical database of patients with colorectal cancer from Chinese population to provide information for early screening and diagnosis， prognostic evaluation， postoperative recurrence monitoring， individualized medication， efficacy evaluation， and drug resistance analysis for patients with CRC， we launched the ChangKang project. Here， as part of the ChangKang Project， we performed ultra-deep whole exome sequencing (WES) of more than 1000 patients with CRC.
